transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I’m just tired all the time and don’t have the energy to do much of anything anymore, even the stuff I used to enjoy. It feels like I'm just going through the motions every day, and I can't seem to shake this constant exhaustion.
Can you tell me more about how you've been feeling emotionally, such as whether you've been experiencing sadness, hopelessness, or a lack of interest in activities you once enjoyed?

Most days I just feel this low, gray cloud hanging over me, and I catch myself thinking, "what's the point?" even when I'm out fishing or sitting with my grandkids. Things I used to love, like working on vintage computers or volunteering with the youth robotics club, now just feel flat or like chores I have to force myself to do.

Can you tell me how long you've been feeling this way, is it something that started recently or has it been going on for a while, and have you had any periods in the past where you felt similar to this?

This low, worn-out feeling really settled in not long after I started phasing into retirement about three years ago, and it has pretty much stuck with me continuously since then. I've never really experienced periods like this in the past before I retired.
Did you notice any significant change in your mood or energy levels during the initial phases of your retirement, or was it more of a gradual decline over the three years since you started retiring?

At the very beginning of my phased retirement, I actually welcomed the change and enjoyed having more time for fishing and gardening. But as the months went by and I struggled to find a sense of purpose, that low energy and gray mood gradually settled in. It has pretty much stuck with me for the last couple of years.

You mentioned that this low, worn-out feeling has been continuous for about three years, but can you tell me if there have been any periods, even brief, where your mood and energy levels returned to normal, or has it been a persistent state?
No, I really haven't had any breaks from it. Once that gray cloud settled in, it has been a constant, daily state without any periods where I felt back to my normal self.
Can you confirm if you've had two or more years with this persistent low mood and lack of energy, or has it been less than two years?

Yes, it has definitely been more than two years. This low, worn-out feeling settled in shortly after I started my phased retirement a little over three years ago, and it has pretty much stuck with me constantly for about two and a half years now.
You've mentioned that this low, worn-out feeling has been constant for about two and a half years. Have you experienced any significant weight loss or gain, or changes in appetite during this time?

Ever since I stopped working full-time, my appetite has been all over the place. Some days I realize it’s three in the afternoon and I’ve barely eaten a sandwich because I just don’t feel interested in food, and then other nights I’ll mindlessly plow through a bag of chips in front of the TV even though I’m not really hungry.

Can you tell me more about what you mean by things feeling 'flat' when you're doing activities you used to enjoy, like is it that you don't get any pleasure from them at all, or is it more that you just can't muster the energy to care about them?

It’s really a combination of both. My internal battery constantly feels like it’s at half-power, which makes hobbies like working on old computers or helping the robotics club feel like chores I have to drag myself through. Even when I do force myself to do them, or spend time with my grandkids, that gray cloud is always there and I find myself thinking "what’s the point?" since I just can't find any real excitement or pleasure in them anymore.
Do you often find yourself feeling guilty or worthless, or are these feelings of 'what's the point' more related to a lack of interest and pleasure in activities?

The "what's the point" feeling is mainly a lack of interest and excitement, where nothing feels worth getting excited about anymore, even fishing or being with my grandkids. I don't really feel deep guilt, but I do struggle with feeling like I'm not useful anymore and have lost my sense of purpose since retiring.

Can you describe if there are any times or situations where you do experience some pleasure or relief from your low mood, even if it's brief, or if the feeling of emptiness and lack of interest is always present?

No, there really aren't any times where I get relief; the low mood and lack of interest are pretty much constant. Even when I do things I used to love, like fishing, being with my grandkids, or volunteering with the robotics club, I don't feel any real pleasure. Those activities just end up feeling like exhausting chores where I constantly catch myself thinking, "what's the point?"

You've mentioned that you don't feel pleasure in activities you used to enjoy, but can you tell me if there are any specific things that still bring you even a little bit of joy or satisfaction, no matter how small it may seem?

Honestly, it’s very difficult to find any genuine joy or satisfaction in anything right now. Even during things that should bring me happiness, like fishing, tinkering with vintage electronics, or being with my grandkids, that gray cloud is always there. It just feels like I'm going through the motions or pushing myself through a chore.

You've described a persistent low mood and lack of interest for over two years, but can you tell me if you've experienced any brief periods, even just a few days, where your symptoms significantly improved or worsened, or has it been a steady state?

It has been a very steady state, with no real ups or downs. This low, worn-out feeling has pretty much stuck with me constantly since it settled in after my retirement, without any periods where it improved or went away.

You've mentioned a steady state of low mood and lack of interest for over two years without significant improvement or worsening, but can you confirm if you've ever had any periods in your life before retirement where you experienced similar feelings of low mood and lack of interest, even if they were shorter-lived?

No, I’ve never experienced anything like this before in my life. Throughout my years working full-time, I always had plenty of energy and never dealt with this kind of persistent low mood. It really only began after I started transitioning into retirement.
Have you experienced any significant depressive episodes that lasted for less than two months at any point in your life, or has your current state been the only prolonged experience of this nature?

No, I have never had any short depressive episodes in the past. This current low, worn-out state is the first and only time I've ever felt this way, and it has been continuous since I started phasing into retirement about three years ago.

You've described a persistent low mood for over two years without significant improvement, but can you confirm if you've had any brief periods of normal mood or if the low mood has been present every day for the past two and a half years?

Yes, I can confirm that. This low, gray feeling has been pretty much constant almost every single day since I started phasing into retirement over two years ago. I haven't had any periods where I felt back to my normal self, and most days I'm just going through the motions under that same cloud.

You've had a persistent low mood for over two years, but can you tell me if there have been any subtle variations in the intensity of your symptoms over time, or has it been a completely uniform experience?

It has been a completely uniform experience. Since it settled in after I started retirement, this low, gray cloud has pretty much stuck with me the entire time without any real breaks or noticeable variations where I felt like my old self.

Have you experienced any significant changes in your social interactions or relationships since you started feeling this way, such as withdrawing from social activities or feeling disconnected from friends and family?

Yes, I've definitely withdrawn from a lot of things over the last couple of years. I've backed out of community commitments, like volunteering with the youth robotics club and going to church concerts, because they just started feeling like exhausting chores. I even feel disconnected and unexcited when I'm spending time with my grandkids, constantly catching myself thinking, "what's the point?"
